pr_title: Add support for customising the creation of Kestrel listen sockets
pr_body:
Fixes #32794. As mentioned in the issue it is currently not possible to configure the underlying listen socket used by Kestrel. In certain circumstances it is desirable to be able to configure socket options when the socket is created - a concrete case that I recently came across is setting the `SO_RECV_ANYIF` socket option on macOS so that Kestrel can listen on the `awdl0` interface (more details on that specific case [here](https://bakedbean.org.uk/posts/2021-05-airdrop-anywhere-part-3/)).

This change adds the API suggested by #32794 by adding a function that allows the caller to manage the creation of the listening socket - `Func<EndPoint, Socket> CreateListenSocket { get; set; }` allows the creation of the listen socket to be configured.

There's also some tests using IPv4, IPv6, unix domain sockets and file handles.

I wonder if it wouldn't be better to change ConfigureListenSocket from `Action<EndPoint, Socket>` to `Func<EndPoint, Socket>`.  If we went this route, we'd want to expose a `Socket CreateListenSocket(EndPoint)` method somewhere and document it with these callbacks.
Create seems like a different scenario from augmentation, and requires more from the implementer.

> and requires more from the implementer.

Not really given `Socket CreateListenSocket(EndPoint)` exists.

> > and requires more from the implementer.
> 
> Not really given `Socket CreateListenSocket(EndPoint)` exists.

Are you saying that this method _would_ exist when moving to a `Func`? I can’t see anything existing like this method except `CreateListenSocket` in libuv that returns a `UvStreamHandle`:  https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Servers/Kestrel/Transport.Libuv/src/Internal/Listener.cs#L49
@halter73 how do you "call base" for the listen socket.
Is CreateDefaultListenSocket supposed to be static?
Yea it should be the stateless default.

Yeah. It should be static. I think it would basically be the current implementation [SocketConnectionListen.Bind()](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Servers/Kestrel/Transport.Sockets/src/SocketConnectionListener.cs#L87-L140), but instead of calling `Socket.Listen(int)` and setting `_listenSocket`, it would return the Socket before listening. The new implementation of `Bind()` would then call the `SocketTransportOptions.CreateListenSocket(EndPoint)` Func and then call `Socket.Listen(int)` on the returned value and set it to `_listenSocket`.

We might have to bypass the CreateListenSocket for FileHandleEndPoints since I can't think of a great way to manage the `_socketHandle` in that case. I think this is fine because if you're using a FileHandleEndPoint, you can configure the socket options before passing it to `KestrelServerOptions.ListenHandle(long)`.

If we make it non-static, we *could* do some trickery where the SocketConnectionListener adds an internal reference to itself to SocketTransportOptions before calling the CreateDefaultListenSocket callback allowing CreateDefaultListenSocket to set `_socketHandle` if need be. Not sure if this would be worthwhile, but I do like that it makes it work in all cases.

We could also make CreateListenSocket a `Func<EndPoint, Func<EndPoint, Socket>, Socket>` and do away with CreateDefaultListenSocket.

> We might have to bypass the CreateListenSocket for FileHandleEndPoints since I can't think of a great way to manage the `_socketHandle` in that case. I think this is fine because if you're using a FileHandleEndPoint, you can configure the socket options before passing it to `KestrelServerOptions.ListenHandle(long)`.

Does the `_socketHandle` field need to be there? It's only used during disposal, but that handle is created with `ownsHandle: true` which, when passed to `Socket`, means the handle is cleaned up in the finaliser of the socket (which arguably is more correct because it's an unmanaged resource). https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/Socket.cs#L3262

That said, is the handle _really_ owned in this case? The user is passing an opaque handle created elsewhere - is it intentional that it is marked as "owned" by the socket transport? Shouldn't they be responsible for cleanup?

Reason I ask - not having that field allows `CreateDefaultListenSocket` to work for all cases and keeps things decoupled (no need to do mess with references to the `SocketConnectionListener` in the instance case).

I've updated to use the triaged API (using a static `CreateDefaultListenSocket`). I removed the `_socketHandle` in the last commit and, so far as I can tell, there are no negative consequences (tests pass, at least). Details (from the commit):

> Note that during implementation I removed the `_socketHandle` field from `SocketConnectionListener` - this was only set so that `Dispose` could be called when the listener is disposed. Under the hood `Socket` already disposes a handle passed to it during finalization, but only if the `ownsHandle` parameter is `true` . In this case the `SafeSocketHandle` _is_ instantiated with  this parameter so the the underlying handle will be closed when the `_listenSocket` field is disposed - that is currently the case when the listener is disposed or unbound.
@halter73 Static method is new as well for API review?
Yes. This is still `api-ready-for-review`. We shouldn't merge before it's approved.

@BrennanConroy currently the implementation of `CreateDefaultListenSocket` does not call `Bind` - the connection listener does it - with the approved API it implies that it should be called - presumably the implementation should be changed to do so?
I've updated the code to match the API review. Let me know if you want any additional tweaks @BrennanConroy
@BrennanConroy @halter73 is this good?
Thanks @deanward81!
Did we measure the perf impact of that change? Asking for a friend :/

@sebastienros We didn't measure the perf of this change, but I'd be shocked if this had a perf impact. This moves the creation of the *listen* socket (not the accepted socket) to a Func, but keeps the logic the same by default. Even if there was a perf hit from calling a Func, it's only called once per address at app startup.

#34769 would be more likely to affect `Connection: close` perf because it touches a per-connection code path. I don't think we explicitly perf tested that. However, it's basically just a refactoring, so it shouldn't impact perf.

issue_context.title: Configure the Accept Socket
comments: It would need to be some kind of callback on the SocketTransportOptions. Features only come into play after accepting a connection.
Alternatively, how about a `KestrelServerOptions.Listen()` overload that accepts a listen socket?

Yeah. A Socket overload to Listen might also be interesting.

One advantage to doing this as a server feature is that it would work with our normal address binding logic, but then we'd probably want to introduce a way to interact with the socket between binding and listening. I'm not sure how we'd do that.

That is a pretty good way to do that. Nice suggestion @Tratcher 😄 I think we should call it `ConfigureListenSocket` to disambiguate between the connection socket being accepted vs the listen socket we're calling accept on.

I wanted to play with .NET 6 in my side project (from the blog post) so added both `ConfigureListenSocket` and `ConfigureAcceptSocket` to test my AirDrop shennanigans with. Seems to be working well on my end so I just added a PR for it.

review_comments: I think it's fine to remove this since we probably shouldn't have taken ownership of the handle in the first place, but I want to point out to other reviewers this is a behavioral change.

```suggestion
                        new SafeSocketHandle((IntPtr)fileHandle.FileHandle, ownsHandle: false)
```

Since we're not managing the lifetime anymore.

Interestingly, when I do this, the test case that uses a `FileHandleEndPoint` never returns - the shutdown of Kestrel hangs indefinitely (when calling `_transportManager.StopAsync()`) - presumably because the underlying socket isn't closed. In the case of the test this is because the underlying `Socket` I steal the handle from is static and I'm unable to manage its lifetime as it's consumed using `MemberData`.

I can absolutely fix the test case but I'm now dubious to change it because it's possible that Kestrel might hang if the caller doesn't clean-up the handle that they supposedly own. That seems like a bad place to be without much indication what the problem is.
Thinking that adding a comment and leaving the `ownsHandle: true` might be a safer route to go here

This makes me think we should just go the `Func<EndPoint, Func<EndPoint, Socket>, Socket>` route since it's the most-flexible/least-tricky way to do this while continuing to manage `_socketHandle` lifetime. This is a pretty advanced API anyway. I don't like the idea of SafeHandle's finalizer controlling the lifetime of the socket.

Actually, it looks like Socket itself disposes the SafeSocketHandle if we claim ownership. It seems like we were doing a bunch of work for nothing. I think your change is good as is. Maybe just add a comment saying that `ownsHandle` indicates the [Socket itself will dispose the handle when it is Disposed](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/999c9c0bf1162e624533e2df58062d2811961fd3/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/Socket.cs#L3270).
